entries.problem_statement: Compute n! (factorial) for non-negative integer n, with 0! = 1 and n! = 1×2×…×n for n ≥ 1.
input_assumptions: Return type is numeric (int) suitable for template test values
boundary_cases: Recursive vs iterative templates must agree on base-case handling for n=0 and n=1

provenance.author: phase13_authoring_packet
provenance.notes: Standard factorial definition; reviewer confirms each template's base case and loop/recursion bounds.

entries.problem_statement: Compute the n-th Fibonacci number F(n) for integer n ≥ 0, with F(0)=0 and F(1)=1, and F(n)=F(n-1)+F(n-2) for n≥2.
input_assumptions: n is a non-negative integer within practical recursion/iteration limits for template tests
Indexing is 0-based: fibonacci(0) returns 0, fibonacci(1) returns 1
boundary_cases: Small n used in bundled tests (e.g. 2, 5, 10)
Clarify behavior for negative n if any template accepts it (default: out of scope / undefined for this family)

provenance.author: phase13_authoring_packet
provenance.notes: Standard Fibonacci definition for reviewer confirmation against each template's function name and base-case policy.

entries.problem_statement: Given two integers a and b, return their greatest common divisor (GCD) using the usual mathematical definition for integers (typically non-negative inputs in beginner templates).
input_assumptions: Inputs are integers; templates may assume a,b ≥ 0 unless stated otherwise
gcd(0, b) and gcd(a, 0) follow template conventions (reviewer to confirm against bundled tests)
boundary_cases: Euclidean vs iterative subtraction variants must match template tests

provenance.author: phase13_authoring_packet
provenance.notes: Standard GCD family description; reviewer must read each template's tests for zero-handling and sign policy.

entries.problem_statement: Given a sequence lst and a target value, return the index of the first occurrence of target in lst, or -1 if target is not present.
input_assumptions: lst is a finite indexable sequence (typically a Python list)
Comparison uses standard equality (==) on elements
Return type is int index or -1
entries.expected_output_summary: First index i with lst[i] == target, else -1.
boundary_cases: Empty list (expect -1 unless target matches empty-list convention — confirm per template)
Target at index 0 and at len(lst)-1

provenance.author: phase13_authoring_packet
provenance.notes: Standard linear search semantics; reviewer must align with each template's parameter names and empty-list tests.

entries.problem_statement: Given a string s, determine whether s reads the same forward and backward (a palindrome). Comparison is case-sensitive unless a problem variant explicitly states otherwise.
input_assumptions: s is a Python str (Unicode code points compared in order)
For this benchmark family, empty string is treated as a palindrome
entries.expected_output_summary: Return True if s is a palindrome, else False.
boundary_cases: Non-palindrome with shared prefix/suffix (e.g. aba vs abba)

provenance.author: phase13_authoring_packet
provenance.notes: Authored from standard palindrome definition for human review. Not derived from faulty student mutations or generator pass/fail outcomes.
